variations.name: Alkaline electrolyzers (incl. pressurized and advanced-membrane designs)
variations.description: Century-old technology that splits water in a liquid potassium hydroxide electrolyte using cheap nickel-based electrodes, making it the lowest-capex and most widely deployed route to green hydrogen at gigawatt scale.

companies.name: Stargate Hydrogen

variations.name: PEM electrolyzers

companies.name: Siemens Energy

companies.name: Ohmium

companies.name: Hystar

companies.name: Quest One (formerly H-TEC Systems)

companies.name: Bosch

variations.name: Solid oxide and proton-conducting ceramic electrolyzers (high-temperature)

companies.name: Topsoe
companies.what: Danish catalysis major industrializing SOEC stacks for e-fuel and ammonia plants
companies.signal: Inaugurated Europe's largest SOEC factory (Herning, 500 MW/yr, €94M EU Innovation Fund) in 2025; paused US factory and cancelled a 100 MW order in 2026 as projects slipped

companies.name: Sunfire
companies.what: German maker of both SOEC and pressurized alkaline; supplied 100 MW alkaline plus multi-MW SOEC demos
companies.signal: €500M+ raised incl. €200M+ Series E and EIB debt; building 100 MW-class electrolysis for RWE Lingen; GW factory plans EU-funded

companies.name: Bloom Energy
companies.what: Repurposes its fuel-cell solid-oxide platform as the Bloom Electrolyzer
companies.signal: 4 MW unit at NASA Ames was world's largest SOEC install; 1.8 MW Jeju Island demo with SK ecoplant; company increasingly focused on data-center fuel cells

companies.name: Ceres Power

companies.signal: Licensees Doosan, Delta, Denso, Thermax; 1 MW SOEC demo with Shell Bangalore; Bosch's Feb 2025 exit from its partnership hit shares

companies.name: FuelCell Energy
companies.what: Molten-carbonate incumbent that built a solid-oxide electrolysis platform tested at Idaho National Laboratory (nuclear-coupled HTE)

companies.name: Elcogen
companies.what: Estonian merchant supplier of low-temperature (650°C) solid-oxide cells and stacks to system integrators
companies.signal: ~€140M raised incl. HD Hyundai (€45M) and Baker Hughes; new Tallinn plant scaling to 360 MW/yr

companies.name: Genvia

companies.signal: Pilot manufacturing line in Béziers; demonstrators with cement and steel partners under France 2030 funding

variations.name: AEM electrolyzers
variations.description: Anion-exchange-membrane cells aim to combine PEM's compact, differential-pressure design with alkaline's cheap, PGM-free materials by running an alkaline reaction across a polymer membrane — the cost holy grail if membrane lifetime is solved.

companies.name: Enapter
companies.what: First commercial AEM vendor; thousands of modular 2.4 kW cores shipped, now scaling to MW 'Nexus' systems
companies.signal: Launched 2.5 MW Nexus 2500 (2025); raised ~€12M via capital increase Nov 2025 targeting 2026 break-even; production JV with China's Wolong

companies.name: EvolOH
companies.what: PGM-free, ultra-high-speed roll-to-roll manufacturable AEM stacks ('Clarity') using no exotic materials
companies.signal: $20M Series A (Engine Ventures, NextEra, 3M); Lowell, MA plant sized toward 3.75 GW/yr; 500 MW stack supply deal Dec 2024; commercial manufacturing started Oct 2025

companies.name: Versogen
companies.what: Univ. of Delaware spinout (Yushan Yan) making durable PiperION AEM membranes and PGM-free stacks
companies.signal: $14.5M Series A led by Doosan/HyAxiom; scaling MW-class pilot stacks

companies.name: Cipher Neutron
companies.what: Canadian developer of 5-250 kW PGM-free AEM stacks for green hydrogen and reversible fuel-cell use
companies.signal: Partnership with TSX-listed dynaCERT; early commercial units and university pilots

variations.white_space: Only a handful of credible players because pure-water-fed AEM membranes still degrade too fast for 60,000-hour industrial duty — the physics bottleneck is hydroxide-induced polymer breakdown; whoever proves a long-life membrane (Ionomr-class chemistry plus a stack integrator) captures PEM performance at alkaline cost, with no iridium supply ceiling.

variations.name: Novel electrolysis architectures (capillary-fed, decoupled, membraneless, supercritical, mid-temperature vapor, direct seawater)
variations.description: A wave of startups re-architects the electrolysis cell itself — capillary feeds, decoupled O2/H2 steps, supercritical water, industrial-steam feeds, or raw seawater — chasing step-change efficiency or capex gains that incremental PEM/alkaline improvement cannot reach.

companies.name: Hysata
companies.what: Australian capillary-fed alkaline cell eliminating bubbles for ~95% system efficiency (41.5 kWh/kg)
companies.signal: US$111M Series B (2024, bp Ventures, Templewater); 5 MW commercial-scale demo with Stanwell; ACWA Power deal (Feb 2025) for Saudi demonstrations

companies.name: H2Pro
companies.what: Israeli E-TAC/decoupled water electrolysis producing H2 and O2 in separate steps — no membrane, ~10-15% better efficiency than PEM
companies.signal: ~$180M raised incl. $75M Series B (2024; BEV, Temasek, Hyundai, ArcelorMittal); MW-scale systems in validation

companies.name: Supercritical Solutions
companies.what: UK membraneless electrolyzer operating in supercritical water, targeting 42 kWh/kg and high-pressure H2 delivery
companies.signal: £14M Series A (Mar 2025) co-led by Shell Ventures and Toyota Ventures; UK government-funded distillery (WhiskHy) and green ammonia projects

companies.name: Advanced Ionics

companies.name: sHYp

companies.name: De Nora

companies.name: Mott Corporation

companies.name: H2U Technologies
companies.what: Caltech-spinout high-throughput discovery platform for non-iridium OER catalysts
companies.signal: Raised ~$11M (2023, incl. TDK Ventures, Freeport); little public progress since — viability unclear

variations.name: Methane pyrolysis (turquoise hydrogen)

companies.name: Monolith

variations.name: Natural (geologic/white) hydrogen exploration
variations.description: Prospecting for hydrogen generated naturally underground by water-rock reactions (serpentinization) and radiolysis — if commercial accumulations prove out, it would be a primary energy source with potential sub-$1/kg cost and near-zero footprint.

companies.name: Koloma

companies.name: Snowfox Discovery

companies.name: HyTerra

companies.name: Gold Hydrogen

companies.signal: Well tests recorded ~95% hydrogen purity plus commercial-grade helium; pilot production studies underway

companies.name: Hydroma

companies.name: 45-8 Energy
companies.what: French explorer pairing helium with native hydrogen across European permits
companies.signal: Holds France's first H2+He exploration licenses (Lorraine, Pyrenees); EU-supported drilling planned

companies.name: Natural Hydrogen Energy
companies.what: Drilled the first dedicated US natural-hydrogen borehole (Nebraska, 2019)
companies.signal: Pioneer with little public activity since; founder Viacheslav Zgonnik remains a sector evangelist

variations.name: Stimulated (orange) and subsurface-biological hydrogen
variations.description: Rather than hunting existing accumulations, these players manufacture hydrogen underground — injecting catalyst-bearing fluids into iron-rich rock to accelerate serpentinization, or feeding microbes in depleted oil reservoirs — turning geology itself into the reactor.

companies.name: Vema Hydrogen
companies.what: Injects catalyst-bearing brine into shallow iron-rich formations to stimulate hydrogen generation at claimed <$1/kg
companies.signal: $13M seed (Feb 2025, Extantia + Propeller); developing first full-scale stimulated-hydrogen pilot wells in North America

companies.name: Gold H2 (Cemvita spinout)
companies.what: Injects engineered microbes into depleted oil wells to bioconvert residual hydrocarbons into hydrogen in situ
companies.signal: Permian Basin field trial measured H2 three orders of magnitude above baseline; spun out of Cemvita as dedicated subsidiary

companies.name: Eden GeoPower
companies.what: Electrical reservoir stimulation to enhance permeability and reaction rates in iron-rich rock for hydrogen generation
companies.signal: ARPA-E-funded serpentinization work; core stimulation business spans geothermal and mining

variations.white_space: Barely three credible players because the chemistry is unproven at field scale: serpentinization kinetics are slow, catalyst delivery and hydrogen recovery from the same wellbore is an unsolved engineering loop, and there is no offtake infrastructure at remote sites. ARPA-E seeded the science in 2024; the opening is for oilfield-services-grade execution (drilling, stimulation, downhole separation) married to geochemistry — a natural play for service majors or well-capitalized spinouts.

variations.name: Blue hydrogen with CCS and novel reforming
variations.description: Reforms natural gas to hydrogen while capturing 90-99% of the CO2 — via ATR/POX with capture, oxy-combustion cycles, membrane reactors or electricity-free solid-oxide conversion — the only route currently capable of megaton-scale low-carbon hydrogen for industry.

companies.name: Air Products
companies.what: World's largest hydrogen producer; building the $7B+ Louisiana Clean Energy Complex (ATR + >95% capture)
companies.signal: Louisiana project delayed to ~2028-29 and descoped under new CEO as company cancelled several US clean-H2 projects in 2025

companies.name: ExxonMobil
companies.what: Baytown plant designed for 1 Bcf/day hydrogen with ~98% capture — would be the world's largest low-carbon H2 facility
companies.signal: FID slipped amid 45V policy uncertainty; ADNOC/XRG agreed 35% equity stake; Air Liquide partnership for O2/N2

companies.name: Shell
companies.what: Operates Quest (Alberta), one of the longest-running blue-hydrogen CCS projects
companies.signal: ~1 Mt CO2/yr captured since 2015 at its Scotford hydrogen units; Polaris expansion FID'd

companies.name: Linde
companies.what: Builds and operates on-site ATR/SMR-with-capture complexes, incl. the $1.8B+ Beaumont, TX plant supplying OCI's blue ammonia
companies.signal: Beaumont complex started up 2025; multiple US Gulf Coast clean-H2 supply schemes

companies.name: 8 Rivers
companies.what: 8RH2 oxy-combustion/CO2-convective reforming claiming >99% capture without amine systems
companies.signal: First commercial deployment announced: Cormorant Clean Energy (Port Arthur, TX) for 880 kt/yr ultra-low-carbon ammonia; FID timing has slipped from Q1 2025

companies.name: Utility Global
companies.what: eXERO electricity-free solid-oxide process converting steel off-gases and other streams directly into hydrogen
companies.signal: $53M Series C (2024; OPG, ArcelorMittal XCarb, Aramco Ventures; ~$178M total); first H2 ever produced from blast-furnace gas in one reactor; first commercial H2Gen units targeted 2026 incl. ArcelorMittal Brazil

companies.name: H2SITE
companies.what: Palladium-membrane reactors that reform or crack ammonia/methanol/biogas and separate pure H2 in a single unit
companies.signal: €36M Series B (Jan 2025, Hy24, BEV, Equinor Ventures); EIC-funded 1 t/day ammonia cracker at a NW-European port

companies.name: Syzygy Plasmonics
companies.what: Light- and electricity-driven photocatalytic reactors for ammonia cracking and low-carbon reforming (now also biogas-to-SAF)
companies.signal: $76M Series C; demo cells with Lotte/Sumitomo in Korea; NovaSAF biogas project in Uruguay

companies.name: Proton Technologies
companies.what: In-situ subsurface combustion of heavy-oil reservoirs with downhole palladium membranes producing 'clear' hydrogen, leaving carbon underground
companies.signal: Saskatchewan Superb field test site; minimal public progress since ~2023 — commercial viability unclear

variations.name: Biomass and waste-to-hydrogen (gasification and non-combustion reforming)
variations.description: Converts municipal waste, biomass or forestry residues into hydrogen via plasma or steam/CO2 gasification and chemical looping — potentially carbon-negative when paired with CO2 storage, and paid twice via tipping fees plus hydrogen sales.

companies.name: Raven SR
companies.what: Non-combustion steam/CO2 reforming of organic waste to hydrogen at closed landfill sites
companies.signal: Received final air permit Nov 2025 for $75M Richmond, CA facility (99 t/day waste → ~2,400 t H2/yr) with Chevron; investors incl. ITOCHU, Samsung Ventures; groundbreaking early 2026

companies.name: SGH2 Energy
companies.what: Solena plasma-enhanced gasification of waste paper into 'greener-than-green' hydrogen (Lancaster, CA flagship)
companies.signal: Permits approved Feb 2023 but no construction/FID announced since — project appears stalled

companies.name: Boson Energy
companies.what: Plasma-assisted gasification of non-recyclable waste into hydrogen 'energy hubs' for EV fast-charging and industry, with mineralized CO2
companies.signal: Siemens partnership; pipeline of first plants in Sweden/Poland/Germany toward claimed 300 plants by 2030 — none yet operating

companies.name: Mote
companies.what: Gasifies forestry waste into hydrogen while geologically sequestering the biogenic CO2 (carbon-negative BECCS-H2)
companies.signal: $7M Series A first close (Mar 2025); Bakersfield and SMUD/Sacramento projects targeting operations 2027-28

companies.name: Babcock & Wilcox
companies.what: BrightLoop chemical-looping process converting biomass or waste fuels to hydrogen with inherent CO2 separation
companies.signal: First commercial-demonstration BrightLoop plant built in Massillon, Ohio; Wyoming and Louisiana projects in development

companies.name: Ways2H
companies.what: Japanese-licensed thermochemical conversion of MSW and medical waste to hydrogen in modular units
companies.signal: Tokyo and California pilots circa 2020-2022; little public activity since — status unclear

variations.white_space: Waste gasification has a 20-year graveyard (capex blowouts, feedstock contamination, syngas cleanup), and the two US flagships illustrate it — SGH2 stalled post-permit and Ways2H went quiet. The economics only close when tipping fees, LCFS/45V credits and hydrogen revenue stack; the opening is modular, non-combustion designs at existing landfill/utility sites with a creditworthy waste partner (the Raven SR–Republic–Chevron template).

variations.name: Biological, photocatalytic, solar-thermochemical and metal-water hydrogen routes
variations.description: Frontier routes that skip electrolysis entirely — engineered microbes fermenting crop waste, sunlight-driven photocatalysts splitting water directly, high-temperature solar redox cycles, and aluminum-water reactions that release hydrogen from scrap metal.

companies.name: HydGene Renewables
companies.what: Engineered biocatalyst (dark fermentation) converting agricultural residues into on-site, on-demand carbon-negative hydrogen
companies.signal: A$6M seed (Agronomics, CEFC) plus A$2.5M NSW grant (2025); pilot ran continuously >2 years, producing high-purity H2 from wheat straw (Mar 2026)

companies.name: Sparc Hydrogen
companies.what: JV (Sparc Technologies, Fortescue, Univ. of Adelaide) running the world's first on-sun photocatalytic water-splitting pilot using concentrated solar
companies.signal: Roseworthy pilot opened Jun 2025; sustained hydrogen production achieved Dec 2025; A$2.75M federal AEA grant

companies.name: SunHydrogen
companies.what: Photoelectrochemical nanoparticle panels generating hydrogen directly from sunlight and water
companies.signal: OTC-listed; square-meter-scale demonstration modules with university and industrial partners (incl. Honda R&D collaboration); pre-revenue

companies.name: Found Energy
companies.what: Catalytically reacts scrap aluminum with water to deliver hydrogen plus steam/heat for industry, using waste metal as an energy carrier
companies.signal: $12M seed; switched on the largest-ever aluminum-water reactor in 2025 (MIT Technology Review); US Army funding ecosystem ($20M Georgia Tech-led program) validating the route

companies.name: Electro-Active Technologies
companies.what: ORNL-spinout microbial electrolysis converting food waste into hydrogen at the bin
companies.signal: Won early DOE/incubator awards (~2019-2022); minimal public activity since — status unclear

variations.white_space: Sparse because the physics is brutal: photocatalysis sits at ~1-5% solar-to-hydrogen versus ~10% needed to beat PV-plus-electrolysis, fermentation rates cap out on microbial kinetics, and solar thermochemical cycles (Sandia/DLR-class) remain lab projects with no dedicated commercial player after Heliogen's collapse. Credible openings are niche-first: distributed ag-waste hydrogen for fertilizer-dependent farms (HydGene's wedge) and aluminum-water systems for defense/remote power where logistics, not $/kg, set the bar — evidenced by the US Army's $20M program.
